# Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-14 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Definitions

- [statement] Cache size scales with num_ctx and is not changed by weight quantization. For llama3.1:8b at f16 the cache is about 128 KiB per token: 4 GiB at 32,768 tokens, 8 GiB at 65,536; q8_0 at 32,768 tokens is about 2.13 GiB. Sliding-window or shared-KV models (Gemma family) break this formula, so sum the 'llama_kv_cache: size' log lines instead. (low confidence) — https://www.ssdnodes.com/learn/ollama-kv-cache-quantization
- [statement] Running Ollama on Windows as a real system service is not provided by the installer: the docs point to the standalone ollama-windows-amd64.zip (CLI plus NVIDIA libs; add ollama-windows-amd64-rocm.zip for AMD) run via `ollama serve` under a wrapper such as NSSM. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/windows
- [statement] OLLAMA_SCHED_SPREAD is a boolean env var described in source as 'Always schedule model across all GPUs', overriding the prefer-single-GPU default. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/envconfig/config.go · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://knightli.com/2026/04/19/ollama-multiple-gpu-notes/

## Structure and components

- [statement] Total VRAM is weights plus KV cache plus runtime overhead. KV bytes per token = 2 x attention layers x KV heads x head dim x bytes per element (f16 2, q8_0 1.06, q4_0 0.56). Example: Llama 3.1 8B uses 128 KiB per token, about 4.3 GB at 32K context. Runtime overhead is about 0.7 GB at short context, paid per GPU. (medium confidence) — https://computingforgeeks.com/how-much-vram-to-run-llm/ · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://docs.ollama.com/faq
- [statement] On a 24 GB card the auto-sized 32k default context for a 32B Q4 model can push total memory past VRAM, spilling layers to CPU and cutting throughput to about a tenth. Fix: cap OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH or num_ctx. (low confidence) — https://computingforgeeks.com/how-much-vram-to-run-llm/
- [statement] For GPU inference a model should fit fully in VRAM; ollama ps shows the Processor column (100% GPU, 100% CPU, or a CPU/GPU split such as 48%/52%). A split means some layers run on CPU from system RAM and is much slower. (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://hostinger.com/tutorials/ollama-gpu-requirements/
- [statement] Vendor-reported benchmark: gemma3:12b at 128k context on one RTX 4090 went from 48/49 to 49/49 GPU layers and 52.02 to 85.54 tok/s; mistral-small3.2 with image input on two RTX 4090s went from 40/41 to 41/41 layers. The post gives no mechanism detail for multi-GPU gains and does not mention SCHED_SPREAD. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-09-23) — https://ollama.com/blog/new-model-scheduling
- [statement] Multi-GPU does not pool into one fast GPU: layers/tensors are split across devices with cross-device transfer overhead, so its main value is fitting larger models, not linear speedup; forcing a split of a model that fits one GPU can be slower. (medium confidence) — https://knightli.com/2026/04/19/ollama-multiple-gpu-notes/ · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://docs.ollama.com/faq
- [statement] The num_gpu option is a count of layers to offload, not a number of GPUs. (low confidence) — https://glukhov.org/llm-performance/ollama/memory-allocation-in-ollama-new-version/

## How it works

- [statement] When Ollama runs as the macOS application, set environment variables with `launchctl setenv` (e.g. `launchctl setenv OLLAMA_HOST "0.0.0.0:11434"`) and restart the Ollama app. The menu-bar app is launched by launchd, not the shell, so exports in ~/.zshrc are not seen. (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://modelpiper.com/blog/ollama-environment-variables
- [statement] On Windows, change the model directory by setting OLLAMA_MODELS as a user-account environment variable (Settings or Control Panel, 'Edit environment variables for your account'), then quit the tray app and relaunch it from the Start menu or open a new terminal. Same mechanism applies to OLLAMA_HOST. (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/windows · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://docs.ollama.com/faq
- [statement] OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION is automatic by default: Ollama uses Flash Attention when the selected backend and devices support it. Setting OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1 forces it on and OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=0 disables it. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://www.ssdnodes.com/learn/ollama-kv-cache-quantization
- [statement] ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES selects AMD ROCm GPUs. List devices with `rocminfo`, and use the Uuid when available. An invalid ID such as -1 forces CPU. (low confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/gpu
- [statement] Vulkan is the documented path for GPUs that ROCm does not cover. Per the current docs it is enabled by default when the backend is installed. OLLAMA_VULKAN=0 or GGML_VK_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1 disables all Vulkan GPUs. GGML_VK_VISIBLE_DEVICES takes numeric IDs to select specific Vulkan GPUs. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/gpu · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://www.phoronix.com/news/ollama-0.12.11-Vulkan
- [statement] On a mixed iGPU/dGPU system where the Vulkan iGPU is unstable, keep Vulkan on and set GGML_VK_VISIBLE_DEVICES to the discrete GPU index (for example 1 when Vulkan1 is the discrete GPU). (low confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/gpu
- [statement] Ollama's default context length depends on detected VRAM: under 24 GiB gives 4k, 24-48 GiB gives 32k, 48 GiB or more gives 256k. Larger context raises memory use; OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH on the server process or the app slider overrides it. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/context-length · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://hostinger.com/tutorials/ollama-gpu-requirements/
- [statement] On Linux, the documented install is `curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh`; the manual path extracts ollama-linux-amd64.tar.zst (plus ollama-linux-amd64-rocm.tar.zst for AMD, or the arm64 package) into /usr. When upgrading manually, remove /usr/lib/ollama first. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/linux
- [statement] On Linux the service runs as user `ollama`, so a custom OLLAMA_MODELS directory must be readable and writable by that user (and its parent path traversable). A root-owned /usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models after a sudo install causes 'permission denied' for other apps sharing that path, such as Msty. (medium confidence) — https://docs.msty.app/troubleshooting/linux-issues · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://docs.ollama.com/linux
- [statement] OLLAMA_MAX_QUEUE defaults to 512. The pending channel is buffered to that size; when full a request fails immediately with ErrMaxQueue ('server busy, please try again. maximum pending requests exceeded'), surfaced as HTTP 503. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/server/sched.go, https://www.ssdnodes.com/learn/ollama-num-parallel-and-max-queue
- [statement] When a new model does not fit, the scheduler picks the runner with shortest session duration (refCount 0 first), forces its sessionDuration to 0, unloads it and retries; queued requests are processed in order. If load OOMs with others resident, all other runners are evicted once before retry. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/server/sched.go · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://docs.ollama.com/faq
- [statement] A loaded runner is reloaded (not reused) if options, context shift, adapters, projector differ or the health ping fails, so varying num_ctx or other options per request between callers triggers reloads and cold starts. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/server/sched.go

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] To set server environment variables under systemd, run `sudo systemctl edit ollama.service` (creates /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service.d/override.conf), add `[Service]` plus `Environment="NAME=value"` lines, then `systemctl daemon-reload` and `systemctl restart ollama`. Do not edit the packaged unit file; package updates overwrite it. (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://docs.ollama.com/linux, https://www.centron.de/tutorials/expose-ollama-network-port-hardening
- [statement] To pin a version on Linux, run the install script with `OLLAMA_VERSION=<version>` (pre-releases allowed). Updating is re-running the install script or re-extracting the tarball. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/linux

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Q4_K_M file sizes: Llama 3.1 8B about 4.9 GB, Qwen3 32B about 19.8-20 GB, Llama 3.3 70B about 42.5-43 GB. Q8_0 of Llama 3.1 8B is about 8.5 GB, roughly double Q4_K_M, and Q6_K is about 6.6 GB. (high confidence) — https://hostinger.com/tutorials/ollama-gpu-requirements/ · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://computingforgeeks.com/how-much-vram-to-run-llm/
- [statement] Tier guide at Q4_K_M, 8K context, one request: 7-8B needs about 6-7 GB VRAM (8 GB card), 12-14B about 10-12 GB (16 GB card), 20-32B about 19-24 GB (24 GB card with short context), 70-72B about 47-52 GB (48 GB tight, 80 GB comfortable). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-10) — https://hostinger.com/tutorials/ollama-gpu-requirements/ · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://computingforgeeks.com/how-much-vram-to-run-llm/
- [statement] CPU-only inference holds the model in system RAM. Guidance: about 16 GB RAM for a 4.9 GB 8B Q4 model, 32 GB as headroom for a ~20 GB model paired with an 8 GB GPU. Apple Silicon uses unified memory; about 23-25 GB is usable by Ollama on a 32 GB Mac. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-15) — https://hostinger.com/tutorials/ollama-gpu-requirements/
- [statement] Behind an nginx reverse proxy, rewrite the Host header to localhost:11434 (or list the external hostname in OLLAMA_ORIGINS) to avoid 403 Forbidden; turn off proxy_buffering and raise proxy_read_timeout so streamed generations are not cut at ~60 s. (medium confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://www.centron.de/tutorials/expose-ollama-network-port-hardening
- [statement] Independent single-16GB-GPU test on v0.12.1: for models too big for VRAM, three of four (mistral-small3.2:24b, gemma3:27b, qwen3:32b) shifted slightly more to CPU (e.g. 41%->44%, 28%->29%, 30%->32% CPU); qwen3:30b-a3b unchanged. Contradicts the vendor claim; anecdotal, one machine, unnamed old version. (low confidence) — https://glukhov.org/llm-performance/ollama/memory-allocation-in-ollama-new-version/
- [statement] Diagnose offload with `ollama ps`: the PROCESSOR column shows 100% GPU or a CPU/GPU split; with the new scheduler the vendor says nvidia-smi figures should match ollama ps. (medium confidence) — https://knightli.com/2026/04/19/ollama-multiple-gpu-notes/ · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://ollama.com/blog/new-model-scheduling
- [statement] Ollama exposes no queue-depth metric; ollama ps and /api/ps list loaded models only, so queueing must be inferred client-side from time-to-first-byte or counted 503s. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-11) — https://www.ssdnodes.com/learn/ollama-num-parallel-and-max-queue

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] A quantized K/V cache requires Flash Attention. Without it the runner rejects a quantized V cache with the error 'quantized V cache was requested, but this requires Flash Attention'. Fix: set OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1 explicitly; if the error persists the backend has no flash attention kernel and the cache must stay f16. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-13) — https://www.ssdnodes.com/learn/ollama-kv-cache-quantization · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://docs.ollama.com/faq
- [statement] OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE is a global option: every model runs with the same type. K and V use the same type, and the type cannot be set per model, in a Modelfile, via the API or on the command line. For mixed types the SSD Nodes guide suggests a second Ollama instance on another port. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://smcleod.net/2024/12/bringing-k/v-context-quantisation-to-ollama/, https://www.ssdnodes.com/learn/ollama-kv-cache-quantization
- [statement] Quality measurements are early and come from the feature author's blog: on Qwen 2.5 Coder 7B (2024-12-06) perplexity went from 8.3891 (f16) to 8.3934 (q8_0), +0.0043. Early implementation figures were roughly +0.002 to +0.05 for q8_0 and +0.206 to +0.25 for q4_0. The author flags embedding models (Ollama tries to detect them and disables quantisation, with a warning), vision models and high-attention-head models (Qwen 2) as possibly more sensitive. (low confidence) — https://smcleod.net/2024/12/bringing-k/v-context-quantisation-to-ollama/
- [statement] Hardware support at introduction: Metal on Apple Silicon, CUDA on Pascal and newer, and most ROCm GPUs. If a model or hardware does not support flash attention, Ollama falls back to f16 and logs a warning. (low confidence) (verified as of 2024-12-04) — https://smcleod.net/2024/12/bringing-k/v-context-quantisation-to-ollama/
- [statement] Upstream llama.cpp CUDA builds compiled without GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS can reportedly fall back silently to CPU attention when flash attention is combined with some quantized K/V combinations (reported: q8_0 K with q4_0 V, head size 512), giving 25-45x slower prefill and no warning. The report is one user's setup, was closed 'not planned' on 2026-07-26 and does not name Ollama builds. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-26) — https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/24485
- [statement] CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES takes a comma-separated list to limit Ollama to a subset of NVIDIA GPUs. UUIDs (from `nvidia-smi -L`) are more reliable than numeric IDs because ordering may vary. An invalid ID such as -1 forces CPU. (low confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/gpu
- [statement] Vulkan cannot read free VRAM unless Ollama runs as root or the binary has cap_perfmon (`sudo setcap cap_perfmon+ep /usr/local/bin/ollama`). Without either, the scheduler uses approximate model sizes. On some Linux distributions the ollama user must also join the render group for AMD GPUs. (low confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/gpu
- [statement] On Linux after a suspend/resume cycle, Ollama can fail to find the NVIDIA GPU and fall back to CPU. Reloading the UVM driver works around it: `sudo rmmod nvidia_uvm && sudo modprobe nvidia_uvm`. (low confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/gpu
- [statement] Slow local vision models may need a longer client-side image timeout than cloud models; the client timeout is separate from the Ollama HTTP request guard. (low confidence) — https://docs.openclaw.ai/providers/ollama/vision.md

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The server reads environment variables once at launch, so a changed OLLAMA_HOST or OLLAMA_MODELS only takes effect after Ollama is restarted. An unparseable port in OLLAMA_HOST logs a warning and silently reverts to the default instead of failing. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-22) — https://modelpiper.com/blog/ollama-environment-variables · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://docs.ollama.com/windows
- [statement] A forum-reported mismatch (phi4-mini showing about 8.9 GB in Ollama against 2.5 GB in a calculator) was explained as weights-only versus weights plus context; calculators that omit context and buffers underestimate real use. (low confidence) — https://forum.level1techs.com/t/ollama-confusion-about-model-size/254525
- [statement] Ollama blog (2025-09-23): the new engine measures the exact memory a model needs before running instead of estimating it; enabled by default for models on the new engine (gpt-oss, llama4, gemma3, qwen3, mistral-small3.2, embedding models and others), with more migrating. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-09-23) — https://ollama.com/blog/new-model-scheduling · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://glukhov.org/llm-performance/ollama/memory-allocation-in-ollama-new-version/
- [statement] Ollama's multimodal support moved to a new in-house engine (announced 2025-05-15) that calls GGML directly from Go instead of relying on llama.cpp for model support. Each model is self-contained and carries its own projection layer, so a failure stays local to that model. (high confidence) — https://ollama.com/blog/multimodal-models · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://www.autodidacts.io/increase-ollama-context-length-num-ctx/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Ollama binds 127.0.0.1 port 11434 by default; the bind address is changed with the OLLAMA_HOST environment variable (for example 0.0.0.0:11434 to listen on all interfaces). (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://modelpiper.com/blog/ollama-environment-variables
- [statement] Default model directories: macOS ~/.ollama/models, Linux (service install) /usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models, Windows C:\Users\%username%\.ollama\models. Setting OLLAMA_MODELS overrides it. (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://docs.ollama.com/macos
- [statement] OLLAMA_ORIGINS controls which browser origins may call the API and is separate from OLLAMA_HOST. Defaults allow 127.0.0.1 and 0.0.0.0 origins; extra origins such as chrome-extension://* must be added explicitly. (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://modelpiper.com/blog/ollama-environment-variables
- [statement] On macOS and Windows the Ollama app registers as a login item at install. It can be disabled (Windows Task Manager Startup apps; macOS Settings, Login Items, 'Allow in the Background'), and the setting is respected across upgrades unless the app is uninstalled. (low confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq
- [statement] The Windows installer does not need Administrator, installs to the home directory by default, and accepts `OllamaSetup.exe /DIR="d:\some\location"` to relocate binaries. Models are stored separately via OLLAMA_MODELS, and uninstalling does not remove models stored at a custom OLLAMA_MODELS location. (low confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/windows
- [statement] App and server logs: macOS ~/.ollama/logs/app.log and server.log; Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\Ollama\app.log and server.log. Models and config live in ~/.ollama (macOS) and %HOMEPATH%\.ollama (Windows). (medium confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/macos · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://docs.ollama.com/windows
- [statement] Official docs document the desktop app's Settings only for context length (launch post, July 2025) and sign-in to Ollama cloud (Settings page on Mac and Windows). Neither the launch post nor the macOS and Windows docs pages mention an app setting for network exposure or model location. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://ollama.com/blog/new-app · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://docs.ollama.com/faq
- [statement] Ollama's HTTP API has no authentication by default; binding OLLAMA_HOST to 0.0.0.0 lets anyone who can reach the port use it. Guard it with a firewall or a reverse proxy such as Nginx (the FAQ shows a proxy config). (medium confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://modelpiper.com/blog/ollama-environment-variables
- [statement] Third-party guides say newer macOS and Windows desktop apps have a Settings toggle 'Expose Ollama to the network'. This came only from search-result snippets; the guide page returned HTTP 403 and no official page confirms it. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.digitalcitizen.life/how-to-expose-ollama-to-the-network-on-windows/
- [statement] OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE sets the K/V cache type. Valid values are f16 (default), q8_0 and q4_0. (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://www.ssdnodes.com/learn/ollama-kv-cache-quantization
- [statement] Per the Ollama FAQ, q8_0 uses approximately 1/2 the memory of f16 with a very small precision loss (recommended if not using f16). q4_0 uses approximately 1/4 the memory with a small-to-medium loss that may be more noticeable at higher context sizes. (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://smcleod.net/2024/12/bringing-k/v-context-quantisation-to-ollama/
- [statement] On systemd installs the variables must be set as Environment= lines on the ollama unit, followed by daemon-reload and restart. Exporting them in a shell does not affect the managed server. A restart unloads all models. (medium confidence) — https://www.ssdnodes.com/learn/ollama-kv-cache-quantization · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://docs.ollama.com/faq
- [statement] Verify the settings on Linux with journalctl -u ollama: the 'llama_kv_cache: size' line shows K (q8_0) / V (q8_0), the 'starting llama-server' line shows --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 --flash-attn on, and the startup config shows OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE:q8_0. ollama ps shows SIZE and CONTEXT. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-13) — https://www.ssdnodes.com/learn/ollama-kv-cache-quantization
- [statement] NVIDIA support needs compute capability 5.0+ and driver 550 or newer. Cards with compute capability 5.0 through 6.2 need driver 570 or newer. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/gpu
- [statement] On Linux, Ollama requires the AMD ROCm v7 driver. On Windows it requires a ROCm v7 / HIP7-capable driver stack. The Windows supported-card list is shorter than the Linux list (Radeon RX 7600 through 7900 XTX and Radeon PRO W7500 through W7900). (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/gpu
- [statement] HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=x.y.z forces ROCm to use a nearby supported LLVM target for an unsupported AMD GPU, for example 10.3.0 for a gfx1032 or gfx1034 card. With mixed GPUs, append the device number (HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION_0, HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION_1). The documented override is Linux-only. (medium confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/gpu · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/2870
- [statement] Vulkan first shipped as experimental. On 2025-11-14 Phoronix reported ollama 0.12.11 with Vulkan enabled by setting OLLAMA_VULKAN=1, aimed at older AMD GPUs without ROCm support and RADV systems without ROCm installed. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-11-14) — https://www.phoronix.com/news/ollama-0.12.11-Vulkan
- [statement] With SELinux, containers may be denied access to AMD GPU devices. Run `sudo setsebool container_use_devices=1` on the host. (low confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/gpu
- [statement] Without HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION, an unsupported gfx1032 card (RX 6650 XT) crashed in rocBLAS with a missing TensileLibrary.dat and a segmentation fault. Setting 10.3.0 in the docker run command fixed it (ollama/ollama:0.1.27-rocm, March 2024). (low confidence) — https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/2870
- [statement] Weight bytes per parameter (Llama 3.3 70B): BF16 2.00, Q8_0 1.06, Q5_K_M 0.71, Q4_K_M 0.60, Q4_0 0.57, IQ4_XS 0.54. Pre-quantized models such as gpt-oss-120b (MXFP4) break this rate, so read the file size instead. (medium confidence) — https://computingforgeeks.com/how-much-vram-to-run-llm/ · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://hostinger.com/tutorials/ollama-gpu-requirements/
- [statement] Required memory scales with OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL x context length: a 2K context with 4 parallel requests becomes an 8K context allocation. Flash attention reduces memory as context grows; quantized KV cache needs flash attention (q8_0 about 1/2 of f16, q4_0 about 1/4). (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://computingforgeeks.com/how-much-vram-to-run-llm/
- [statement] The documented manual systemd setup creates a system user and group `ollama` (home /usr/share/ollama, shell /bin/false), adds the current user to that group, and writes /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service with ExecStart=/usr/bin/ollama serve, User=ollama, Restart=always, RestartSec=3, WantedBy=multi-user.target; then daemon-reload and enable/start. Logs are read with `journalctl -e -u ollama`. (low confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/linux
- [statement] A drop-in saved without the `[Service]` header is silently ignored, and a variable exported in a user shell never reaches the systemd-run daemon (the CLI is only an HTTP client). Verify with `systemctl show ollama.service -p Environment` and `ss -tlnp | grep 11434`. (medium confidence) — https://www.centron.de/tutorials/expose-ollama-network-port-hardening · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://docs.ollama.com/faq
- [statement] Ollama binds 127.0.0.1:11434 by default; OLLAMA_HOST changes the bind address (e.g. 0.0.0.0:11434 for all interfaces, or a single private IP). The API has no built-in authentication or rate limiting, so exposing it needs a firewall source-subnet rule or a reverse proxy with auth and TLS. (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://www.centron.de/tutorials/expose-ollama-network-port-hardening
- [statement] On Windows, OllamaSetup.exe installs per-user without Administrator rights (default under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Ollama, PATH updated for the user); `OllamaSetup.exe /DIR="d:\some\location"` relocates the binaries. Requirements: Windows 10 22H2 or newer and NVIDIA driver 551.61+ for NVIDIA cards. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/windows
- [statement] On Windows, Ollama inherits user and system environment variables. Set OLLAMA_HOST, OLLAMA_MODELS etc. under 'Edit environment variables for your account', then quit the tray application and relaunch it from the Start menu (or open a new terminal). If OLLAMA_MODELS was changed, the uninstaller does not remove downloaded models. (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/windows · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://docs.ollama.com/faq
- [statement] On Windows, logs live in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Ollama (app.log for the GUI, server.log for the server, upgrade.log); models and config default to %HOMEPATH%\.ollama. (low confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/windows
- [statement] Default multi-GPU placement: if the model fits entirely on any single GPU, Ollama loads it on that GPU (less PCIe traffic); only if it does not fit on one GPU is it spread across all available GPUs. (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://knightli.com/2026/04/19/ollama-multiple-gpu-notes/
- [statement] OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD reserves a number of bytes of VRAM per GPU (default 0), shrinking what the scheduler treats as available. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/envconfig/config.go
- [statement] Current envconfig exposes llama.cpp fit controls: LLAMA_ARG_FIT (auto-fit unset memory options, default on) and LLAMA_ARG_FIT_TARGET (free VRAM margin per device, MiB). (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/envconfig/config.go
- [statement] OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL defaults to 1 in envconfig; required memory scales with OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL * OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH (a 2K context with 4 parallel requests becomes 8K). (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/envconfig/config.go, https://www.ssdnodes.com/learn/ollama-num-parallel-and-max-queue
- [statement] OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS: env default is 0, which the scheduler turns into 3 * max(GPU count,1); a model loads concurrently only if it fits in memory, and on GPU must fit fully in VRAM. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/server/sched.go, https://www.glukhov.org/llm-performance/ollama/how-ollama-handles-parallel-requests/
- [statement] Requests for an already-loaded model reuse the runner and skip the pending queue, so the 503 applies to requests needing a model load, not those waiting on a parallel slot. (medium confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/server/sched.go · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://www.ssdnodes.com/learn/ollama-num-parallel-and-max-queue
- [statement] Default keep-alive is 5 minutes. Per-request keep_alive on /api/generate and /api/chat overrides OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE; 0 unloads right after the response, negative (e.g. -1) keeps loaded forever. Env parsing accepts durations or integer seconds; an unparseable value silently keeps 5m. (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama server ops, scheduling, GPU, sizing and desktop · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/envconfig/config.go
- [statement] The scheduler forces numParallel to 1 for embedding models and for some architectures (e.g. mllama, qwen35, lfm2), regardless of OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/server/sched.go
- [statement] On Windows with Radeon GPUs the FAQ says max loaded models defaults to 1 due to ROCm v5.7 VRAM reporting limits (note may be outdated). (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq
